title: TypeScript SDK: Duplex stream bridging conventions and bidirectional examples
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Developers need a single ergonomic set of conventions for handling bidirectional streaming with the TypeScript SDK that interops between AsyncIterator-style consumers and Web Streams (ReadableStream/TransformStream) across Node and browser runtimes. We currently have multiple undocumented patterns that lead to bugs around backpressure, cancellation, and dual-consumer handoffs.

Goal: Deliver a short, prescriptive guide and examples plus runtime helpers so SDK consumers can: 1) obtain streams in both AsyncIterator and ReadableStream forms; 2) compose duplex handlers (send client events while receiving tokens); 3) correctly propagate cancellation and backpressure; 4) apply resumable retry checkpoints for long-running streams. Provide tests and example apps, and one small runtime helper in the SDK to reduce repeated boilerplate.
acceptance_criteria: API surface: sdk.client.stream(request) returns an object exposing .asyncIterator and .webStream hot adapters documented in README
Compatibility: adapters work in Node 18+ and modern browsers (Chromium-based and Firefox) without polyfills in standard bundlers
Backpressure: AsyncIterator<Chunk> consumption pauses source dispatch when consumer is slow (verified in stress tests)
Cancellation: calling iterator.return() or closing the ReadableStream cancels server-side request and frees KV cache quickly (observed in integration tests)
Resumable retries: resume-from-checkpoint pattern demonstrated in an example with deterministic reconsume semantics
Examples: two sample apps (chat duplex + audio streaming) added to examples/ts/streams and referenced in SDK README
Tests: unit tests covering cancellation propagation, dual-consumer guards, and a small e2e test that runs against the staging runtime
technical_notes:
Key design trade-offs considered:
- Option A: Return a single object with lazy adapters vs. separate API calls for AsyncIterator and WebStream. Chosen: single object with .asyncIterator() and .webStream() factory methods to avoid duplicating network setup while keeping lazy instantiation.
- Backpressure: Node AsyncIterator cannot directly observe underlying socket pressure; we implement a small buffering window plus pause/resume semantics via a token-queue and a low/high watermark. This sacrifices strict TCP-level backpressure but gives predictable memory bounds.
- Cancellation: Browser ReadableStream cancel() maps to the same abort controller used by the underlying fetch/transport; iterator.return() also triggers abort. Ensure repeated cancel calls are idempotent.
- Retries: Resumable retries rely on checkpoints emitted from the server (sequence id + KV keys). We'll add helper utilities to encode/decode checkpoints and a runtime hook to attach checkpoint headers on retry. For now retries are opt-in behind an example flag.
implementation_plan: Design API and docstrings: add .asyncIterator() and .webStream() to stream response object
Implement internal TokenQueue with low/high watermark and tests for pause/resume semantics
Wire cancellation: unify AbortController usage between adapters and transport layer
Add checkpoint encoder/decoder helpers and an example resume flow in examples/ts/streams/chat-resumable.ts
Add unit tests for dual-consumer guard (throw when both adapters consumed concurrently unless explicit split mode is used)
E2E: run against staging runtime with artificially throttled consumer to validate backpressure
Docs & examples: README changes + migration note for older patterns
test_plan: Unit: TokenQueue pause/resume under producer burst; memory bound enforcement
Unit: iterator.return() triggers fetch abort and emits 'cancelled' instrumentation event
Integration: webStream.close() causes server-side request cancellation in staging (repro script included)
Stress: simulate 200 concurrent chat streams with slow consumers to observe queuing behavior in CI job
Compatibility: bundle-diff test with esbuild/webpack to ensure no global polyfills required in browser target
rollout_notes: Ship helper API behind minor version bump (sdk-2026.03). Default behavior preserves current non-resumable behavior; examples show opt-in patterns for resumable retries. Notify customers in changelog of new adapters and recommend migration for teams using custom stream shims. We'll enable an experimental flag in the public SDK beta channel for two weeks before flipping to general availability.
comments: 2026-03-01 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after recurring internal support issues where users mis-handle cancellation in the browser. Linked to support case SUP-914.

2026-03-03 Marco Ruiz: Spike implemented token-queue prototype and validated pause/resume in Node. Found that Node's stream.Readable backpressure events are too coarse; we will use an internal bounded queue with async waiters.

2026-03-05 Evan Kim (review): Suggested explicit dual-consumer guard and an escape hatch 'split()' mode where the stream demuxes into two independent branches. Also asked to document cost implications of buffering.

2026-03-06 Marco Ruiz: Implemented cancellation flow using shared AbortController. Verified iterator.return() triggers transport abort and server-side logs show request terminated; added unit test in PR.

2026-03-08 QA: Found intermittent duplicate events when using webStream default reader.read() fast-path; root cause was a race in the token enqueue loop. Fix committed in branch feature/stream-queue-racefix.
2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Design doc published and linked below. Decided not to expose low/high watermarks in public API for now; we'll add telemetry instead.
2026-03-12 Marco Ruiz: Opened PR and requested review from SDK owners. Cutting a small alpha release for internal teams to exercise duplex audio example.
2026-03-12 Lucy Chen (PM): Approved rollout plan; requested short migration guide for platform partners using older SDK versions.
examples: examples/ts/streams/chat-duplex.ts - chat client that sends user events while streaming tokens
examples/ts/streams/audio-duplex.ts - browser audio upload with streaming transcript responses
examples/ts/streams/chat-resumable.ts - demonstrates checkpoint emit + resume logic
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on (1) races in TokenQueue, (2) semantics of iterator.return() vs webStream.cancel(), and (3) public API ergonomics. Perf tests attached; please run the staging e2e job if you review.
